intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, protected waters and rental equipment on-site. An educational video about the reef ecosystem is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in the rich cultures of Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand through live demonstrations, canoe rides, and traditional performances. The evening luau and fire knife dance show is a highlight that kids and adults absolutely love.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a beginner family surf lesson on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered one of the best places in the world to learn to surf. Certified instructors guide kids and adults alike, and most first-timers stand up on their board within the first lesson. Boards and rash guards are included.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive & Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on a breathtaking self-guided road trip along Maui's famous Road to Hana, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and scenic lookouts. Families can swim at Twin Falls and explore the Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach State Park. Pack a picnic and make a full day of this unforgettable adventure.

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch at Helena's Hawaiian Food
experiences.description: Treat the family to an authentic, award-winning Hawaiian plate lunch experience at this legendary James Beard Award-winning restaurant. Enjoy classic dishes like kalua pig, lomi salmon, poi, and haupia (coconut pudding) in a no-frills, local atmosphere that has been serving Hawaii's comfort food since 1946.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront room and get settled.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 via Flight UA. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack from a nearby convenience store or hotel vending machine. Rest and prepare for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab something on the plane
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport food before departure
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a 7-Eleven or ABC Store near the resort (budget-friendly, open late)

day_by_day.notes: Pack light snacks in your carry-on for the late arrival. ABC Stores are a Hawaii staple and usually open late — great for affordable local snacks, drinks, and essentials. Don't forget to confirm check-in details with the resort ahead of time for a smooth late-night arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely morning walk along the beachfront just outside the resort. Watch the sunrise over the ocean — completely free and breathtaking. Take photos and explore the immediate shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach (most Hawaii beaches are free and open to the public). Swim, snorkel with a rented snorkel set (rentals typically $10–$15/day at local shops), and build sandcastles with the family. Look for sea turtles resting on the shore — a common and magical sight.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade or nearby town center. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Hawaii's most iconic free experiences. Return to the resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee from a local farmers market or grocery store like Foodland or Times Supermarket ($5–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or wraps from the grocery store to enjoy on the beach ($3–$5 per person)
meals.dinner: Find a local plate lunch spot — try a Hawaiian plate lunch (rice, mac salad, protein) for $10–$13 per person. Look for L&L Hawaiian Barbecue or a local diner.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at an ABC Store to save money throughout the trip. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect Hawaii's coral reefs. This is a great low-key day to adjust to island time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby state or county park for a family-friendly hike. Look for easy nature trails with scenic overlooks or coastal views. Many Hawaiian state parks are free or charge a minimal parking fee ($5–$10). Bring water and snacks from the grocery store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local farmers market (many run on weekday and weekend mornings through early afternoon). Sample fresh tropical fruits like lychee, mango, and pineapple. Purchase affordable local produce and snacks for the week. Browse handmade crafts for budget-friendly souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the beach for a family sunset picnic. Pick up affordable picnic supplies from the grocery store — fresh fruit, local chips, hummus, and juice boxes for the kids. Enjoy the golden hour on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl from a local cafe or food truck ($8–$12) — a quintessential Hawaiian breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Farmers market snacks and fresh fruit ($10–$15 for the family)
meals.dinner: Grocery store picnic dinner on the beach — deli items, fruit, and drinks ($15–$20 for the family)

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings for free community events, outdoor movies, or cultural performances happening this evening. Many Hawaiian communities host free events in public parks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a free or low-cost cultural or historical site. Look for local heiau (ancient Hawaiian temples), historical museums with free admission days, or cultural centers. Many offer free guided tours or self-guided walking paths that are educational and family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a family-friendly snorkeling beach. Pack your own snacks and water. Look for calm, protected bays with clear water and abundant marine life. Many locals recommend less-touristy beaches for better snorkeling and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local town center or village. Window shop, visit free art galleries, or watch local street performers. Look for a shave ice stand — a must-try Hawaiian treat for $3–$6 per person.

meals.breakfast: Make your own breakfast with grocery store supplies — cereal, milk, bananas, and orange juice ($2–$4 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the snorkeling beach — PB&J sandwiches, chips, and fruit ($3–$5 per person)
meals.dinner: Try a local poke bowl restaurant or food truck. Poke bowls are a Hawaiian staple and budget-friendly at $12–$16 per bowl.

day_by_day.notes: Poke bowls are one of the best budget-friendly local foods in Hawaii. Look for grocery store poke counters (like Foodland) for even more affordable options — often $8–$12 per bowl with rice.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free or low-cost scenic drive along the coast. Pull over at lookout points for panoramic ocean views, dramatic cliffs, and lush valleys. This is a great way to see a lot of the island without spending much — just the cost of gas if renting a car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a scenic waterfall or botanical garden along the route. Many botanical gardens in Hawaii offer free or low-cost admission ($5–$15 per adult, children often free). Kids will love exploring the tropical plants and looking for colorful birds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a beach bonfire if permitted, or relax on the beachfront. Look for a local luau-style community event or free cultural performance in the area.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local bakery for fresh malasadas (Portuguese donuts) — a beloved Hawaii treat at $1–$2 each. Leonard's Bakery is iconic if nearby.
meals.lunch: Roadside food truck or local diner during the scenic drive ($8–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using grocery store ingredients back at the resort if your room has a kitchenette, or grab affordable takeout ($10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a car, compare prices on Turo or discount rental agencies for the best budget rates. Always fill up gas at Costco if you have a membership — significantly cheaper than island gas stations.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — try a new water activity. Look for free or low-cost options like boogie boarding (board rentals $5–$10/hour), paddleboarding, or simply body surfing. Many beaches have gentle waves perfect for beginners and kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local aquarium or marine education center. Many offer discounted family admission rates ($10–$15 per adult, $5–$8 per child). This is a great educational activity for kids to learn about Hawaiian marine life and coral reef ecosystems.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local shopping center or outdoor mall for free entertainment — often features live music, hula performances, or cultural demonstrations, especially on weekends. Great for people-watching and souvenir browsing without pressure to buy.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and granola from a health food cafe or grocery store ($5–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Shrimp truck or garlic shrimp plate — a famous Hawaiian roadside food experience ($12–$15 per plate, shareable for families)
meals.dinner: Local ramen or noodle shop — Hawaii has excellent Asian-influenced cuisine at budget-friendly prices ($10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii's multicultural food scene means you can find delicious, affordable Japanese, Korean, Filipino, and Chinese food throughout the islands. These local spots are often much cheaper than tourist-facing restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip free day at the beach. Relax, swim, and recharge. Build sandcastles, collect shells, or simply enjoy the sound of the waves. This is your family's time to do whatever feels most enjoyable without a schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore tide pools at a rocky beach section. This is a completely free and fascinating activity for kids — look for sea urchins, small fish, crabs, and colorful anemones. Teach kids about the importance of not disturbing marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to a special mid-trip dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant (still budget-conscious). Look for happy hour specials, early bird deals, or local favorites that offer great value. This is a good night to celebrate the halfway point of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a hearty breakfast plate from a local diner — eggs, rice, and spam (a Hawaii staple) for $8–$12 per person
meals.lunch: Pack a beach picnic with grocery store supplies — cold cuts, cheese, crackers, fruit, and juice ($15–$20 for the family)
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant with fresh catch of the day — look for affordable lunch-menu-style pricing or early dinner specials ($15–$20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Spam musubi is a must-try Hawaiian snack — a slice of spam on rice wrapped in seaweed, available at most convenience stores for $1.50–$3. Perfect for beach snacking.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning walk or easy hike to catch the sunrise from a scenic overlook or hilltop. Many trails in Hawaii are free and offer stunning panoramic views of the coastline, mountains, and valleys at golden hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free beach park with picnic facilities. Spend the afternoon swimming, playing beach volleyball, or flying a kite. Many county beach parks have free parking, showers, and restrooms — great for families.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost outdoor movie, community concert, or cultural event. Check local event boards, community Facebook groups, or the Hawaii Tourism Authority website for free events happening this week.

meals.breakfast: Pack a sunrise breakfast — granola bars, fruit, and a thermos of coffee or hot chocolate for the kids ($5–$8 for the family)
meals.lunch: Plate lunch from a local drive-in or takeout spot ($10–$13 per person) — try kalua pork, lomi salmon, or chicken katsu
meals.dinner: Casual pizza or burger spot for a family-friendly and budget-friendly dinner ($10–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check the weather forecast the night before for any outdoor plans. August in Hawaii is generally sunny and warm, but brief rain showers can occur. Always have a backup indoor activity in mind.

day_by_day.morning: Final full adventure day — choose a family favorite activity to revisit. Whether it's snorkeling at the best beach you found, hiking a favorite trail, or exploring a new beach, make it count. Pack a full day bag with snacks, water, and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at local shops, ABC Stores, or a farmers market. Focus on affordable, meaningful souvenirs — locally made macadamia nut products, Hawaiian sea salt, or handmade crafts. Avoid overpriced airport gift shops.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a beloved local restaurant you've been wanting to try all trip. Splurge slightly within budget for a memorable last dinner. Try a traditional Hawaiian plate with poi, laulau, and haupia (coconut pudding) for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a local diner to fuel the final adventure day ($8–$12 per person)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic or food truck lunch at your chosen activity location ($8–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a highly-rated local Hawaiian restaurant ($15–$25 per person — a worthwhile splurge for the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Pack any souvenirs and non-essential items tonight to make tomorrow's departure smoother. Check airline baggage rules to avoid extra fees. Consider shipping bulky items home if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning beach walk or sunrise viewing. Take in the ocean one last time and collect any last memories. Pack remaining belongings and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the hotel concierge if checkout is before your departure time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use remaining time for any last-minute activities close to the resort or airport. Visit a nearby lookout point, grab a final shave ice, or relax at the beach until it's time to head to the airport. Aim to arrive at the airport 2–3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories. Reflect on the trip highlights during the flight. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast — grab a spam musubi and fresh fruit from an ABC Store or local cafe ($5–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or airport area before departure ($8–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food — budget for $10–$15 per person at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Use up any remaining Hawaiian cash or gift cards before departure. Many airports have local food options past security that are better value than chain restaurants. Double-check all rooms, the safe, and common areas before final checkout to ensure nothing is left behind.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (pre-book a shuttle or rideshare to save on taxi costs), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Settle into your room and unwind on the lanai with the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or layover airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack from the resort's lobby bar or a nearby 24-hour convenience store (ABC Stores are ubiquitous in Waikiki)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Hydrate well after the flight, set your alarms for an easy start tomorrow, and resist the urge to explore tonight — you have 9 full days ahead. Confirm resort check-in details in advance since arrival is after 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the ocean and soak up your first full Hawaiian sunrise. Visit the beach directly in front of Aegean Bliss Resort — set up chairs, play in the surf, and let the kids acclimate to the warm Pacific water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (a short walk or drive from the resort) for your first real beach afternoon. Rent boogie boards or snorkel gear from a local beach shack (budget ~$15–$20/person). Explore the shoreline, build sandcastles, and enjoy the iconic Diamond Head backdrop. Walk through Kalakaua Avenue for window shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the Duke Kahanamoku Statue at Waikiki Beach for a classic Hawaii photo moment. Watch the sunset from the beach, then head to dinner at a nearby mid-range restaurant along Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or nearby Eggs 'n Things (famous local breakfast spot, ~$15–$20/person)
meals.lunch: Grab plate lunches from a local food truck near Waikiki Beach (~$12–$15/person)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood or Marukame Udon — casual, affordable, and beloved by locals (~$15–$25/person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule — jet lag may still be a factor, especially for kids. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously; the Hawaiian sun is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a world-class snorkeling experience. Arrive early (open at 6:45 AM) to secure parking and avoid crowds — reservations are required and must be booked online in advance (~$25/adult, kids under 12 free). Watch the mandatory marine education video, then descend to the bay. Snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral in the crystal-clear protected waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapu'u Point Lookout for stunning coastal views. Stop at Makapu'u Beach Park — a beautiful but wave-heavy beach great for photos and picnicking. On the way back, swing through the charming town of Kailua for shave ice at Aoki's Shave Ice (~$5–$8/person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for showers and downtime. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local favorite near the resort. Kids can play on the beach as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing for Hanauma Bay (pack snacks and water for the morning)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch or grab food from a nearby deli/grocery store before Hanauma Bay — no food vendors inside the preserve
meals.dinner: Side Street Inn or Lulu's Surf Club Waikiki — lively, family-friendly atmosphere with generous portions (~$20–$35/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are essential and often sell out weeks in advance — book as soon as possible. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent on-site. Water shoes recommended. The hike down to the bay is moderate — stroller-accessible but can be tiring for very young children.

day_by_day.morning: Today is all about culture! Drive to the Polynesian Cultural Center on Oahu's North Shore (~1 hour from Waikiki). Purchase the Day Pass (~$70–$90/adult, ~$55–$65/child) and spend the morning exploring the six island villages — Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Watch live cultural demonstrations including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Catch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon (usually mid-afternoon), where performers from each island culture showcase their traditions in a vibrant floating parade. Let the kids participate in hands-on activities like spear throwing and hula lessons.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show (included in most day pass packages or available as an add-on). This stunning theatrical production tells the story of a Polynesian family across generations — highly recommended for all ages. Grab dinner at the Center's Ali'i Luau or on-site restaurants before the show.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the drive north
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in some packages or ~$30–$40/adult, great variety of island foods
meals.dinner: Dine at the Polynesian Cultural Center's restaurant before the evening show, or grab a quick meal on the drive back along the North Shore

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is a full-day commitment — plan to spend 8–10 hours there. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The North Shore drive is beautiful; if time allows on the return trip, stop at Ted's Bakery in Sunset Beach for famous cream pies (~$5–$7/slice). Book tickets online in advance for best pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Today is surf day! Head to Waikiki Beach for beginner family surf lessons (~$75–$100/person for a 2-hour group lesson). Waikiki's long, gentle rolling waves are world-renowned as the best place on earth to learn to surf — instructors will have even young children standing on boards within the first lesson. This is an unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surf lessons, enjoy a leisurely afternoon on Waikiki Beach. Grab lunch nearby, then walk to Kapiolani Park — a beautiful 300-acre park adjacent to Waikiki. Visit the Honolulu Zoo (budget-friendly at ~$20/adult, $12/child) or the Waikiki Aquarium (~$12/adult, $5/child) for a fun, educational family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon_alternate: Alternatively, rent bikes from a local shop and cycle the scenic path through Kapiolani Park to Diamond Head.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to an authentic Hawaiian plate lunch dinner experience at Helena's Hawaiian Food — a James Beard Award-winning institution serving traditional kalua pig, lomi salmon, poi, and haupia. This is a must-do culinary experience to understand true Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast burritos or acai bowls from a Waikiki café before surf lessons (~$10–$15/person)
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In — a beloved local institution near Kapiolani Park, famous for plate lunches (~$10–$14/person)
meals.dinner: Helena's Hawaiian Food — traditional Hawaiian plate lunch experience, award-winning and authentic (~$15–$25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons in advance, especially in August which is peak season. Most surf schools on Waikiki accommodate children as young as 5. Apply waterproof reef-safe sunscreen before lessons. Helena's Hawaiian Food can have a wait — arrive early or be prepared to queue; it's absolutely worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike up Diamond Head State Monument (~$5/person entry). The 1.6-mile round-trip trail rewards hikers with panoramic views of Waikiki, the Pacific Ocean, and the Ko'olau Mountains. The hike takes about 1.5–2 hours and is suitable for older children and active families. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum (~$25/adult, $17/child). Explore exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, ancient artifacts, volcanic geology, and Pacific island cultures. The planetarium show is a family highlight. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the resort and enjoy a sunset beach walk. Try shave ice at Waiola Shave Ice — a legendary Honolulu spot beloved by locals. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the Diamond Head hike — pack trail snacks and plenty of water
meals.lunch: Kaimuki neighborhood lunch near the Bishop Museum — try Mud Hen Water or a local plate lunch spot (~$15–$20/person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with great Hawaiian-inspired food and ocean views (~$25–$40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations are now required and can be made online at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Bring plenty of water for the hike — there are no water stations on the trail. The trail includes stairs and tunnels, which kids often find exciting. Flashlights are helpful for the tunnel sections.

day_by_day.morning: Today is a travel day — fly inter-island to Maui (short 30-minute flight, ~$60–$120/person on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest). Check in to a Maui accommodation or use the day as a base from Oahu if staying put. If flying to Maui, pick up a rental car at the airport (essential for the Road to Hana tomorrow). Spend the morning exploring Lahaina town — a charming historic whaling village with art galleries, boutiques, and the famous 150-year-old Banyan Tree.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ka'anapali Beach — consistently ranked among America's best beaches. Snorkel at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) where you can swim alongside sea turtles and colorful fish in calm, clear water. Rent snorkel gear on the beach (~$15/person). The kids will love the gentle conditions here.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a beautiful cultural tradition where a torch lighter runs along the beach and dives from the rock. Enjoy dinner in Lahaina.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Honolulu airport or resort before flying
meals.lunch: Aloha Mixed Plate in Lahaina — casual, open-air restaurant with ocean views and affordable Hawaiian-Asian fusion (~$15–$20/person)
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill or Kimo's Restaurant — mid-range Maui dining with fresh local fish and family-friendly atmosphere (~$25–$40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance for best rates. If staying on Oahu for the full trip, skip the Maui days and substitute with North Shore exploration or additional Oahu activities. A rental car on Maui is non-negotiable for the Road to Hana experience. Book it ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the legendary Road to Hana — one of the world's most spectacular scenic drives. Start early (by 7 AM) to beat traffic on the narrow, winding road. First major stop: Twin Falls (~Mile 2) — an easy 15-minute walk to beautiful waterfall pools perfect for a refreshing swim. Continue to Garden of Eden Arboretum (~$20/car) for stunning valley and ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Road to Hana, stopping at Wai'anapanapa State Park — home to the famous black sand beach, sea caves, and blowholes. Walk the coastal trail for dramatic lava cliff views. Arrive in Hana town for a late lunch. Visit the Pools at 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakala National Park (~$30/car, covers 3 days) — a series of cascading waterfalls and swimming pools set in a lush bamboo forest.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive (or stay overnight in Hana if budget allows — charming but pricier). The drive back takes 2–3 hours. Enjoy a casual dinner back in the Ka'anapali or Lahaina area.

meals.breakfast: Pack a cooler with breakfast items and snacks the night before — stops along the Road to Hana are limited and pricey
meals.lunch: Braddah Hutts BBQ Grill in Hana — a beloved roadside food truck with amazing BBQ plates (~$12–$18/person)
meals.dinner: Fleetwood's on Front Street in Lahaina — rooftop dining with live music and great sunset views (~$25–$40/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is 64.4 miles one-way with 620 curves and 59 bridges — allow a full 10–12 hours for a comfortable experience. Download an offline GPS map or the GyPSy Guide Road to Hana app (~$5) which provides audio narration at each stop. Pack motion sickness medication for children prone to car sickness. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for the Haleakala Sunrise experience — drive to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet) to watch the sun rise above the clouds in one of Hawaii's most spiritual and awe-inspiring settings. Reservations are required ($1/person reservation fee + $30/car park entry). Bring warm layers — summit temperatures can be near freezing even in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Haleakala and stop in Makawao town — a charming upcountry cowboy town with boutique shops and the famous Komoda Store & Bakery for cream puffs and malasadas (~$2–$4 each). Spend the afternoon back at the beach for a final Maui swim. Visit Napili Bay or Kapalua Bay — two of Maui's most beautiful and family-friendly snorkeling beaches with calm, clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell Maui dinner with fresh local fish and Hawaiian flavors. Reflect on the trip with the family over a memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Pack hot drinks and breakfast snacks for the pre-dawn Haleakala drive — no food available at the summit
meals.lunch: Paia Fish Market in Pa'ia town — legendary casual seafood spot with incredible fish tacos and plates (~$15–$22/person)
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House (splurge-worthy special occasion dinner, book months in advance, ~$50–$80/person) OR Café O'Lei at the Maui Golf Club for a more budget-friendly special meal (~$25–$35/person)

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala Sunrise reservations must be made at recreation.gov and often sell out weeks in advance — book immediately. The drive to the summit takes about 1.5 hours from Ka'anapali. Bring jackets, gloves, and blankets for everyone — the cold at the summit surprises most visitors. If sunrise feels too ambitious with kids, the sunset at Haleakala is equally spectacular and requires no reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a slow, savoring breakfast at your favorite local spot. Take one last walk on the beach, collect shells, and let the kids play in the waves. Pack thoughtfully and check out of your accommodation. If flying back from Maui, allow extra time for the inter-island connection back to Honolulu if needed for your departing international flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend any remaining hours at a nearby beach or explore a local farmers market. Visit the Maui Swap Meet (Saturday mornings) or a local craft market for last-minute souvenirs — look for locally made macadamia nut products, Kona coffee, Hawaiian quilts, and aloha wear. Head to the airport with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with hearts full of aloha, sandy toes, and incredible family memories. Review your favorite moments from the trip on the flight home.

meals.breakfast: One last shave ice or acai bowl from a local favorite — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Airport dining or a quick plate lunch near the airport before departure
meals.dinner: On the flight home or at a layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii agricultural inspection is strict — you cannot bring certain fresh fruits, plants, or soil back to the mainland. Pineapples are generally fine; check TSA and USDA guidelines for other items. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for airport check-in, security, and boarding. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases directly home to avoid baggage fees.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, protected waters and rental equipment on-site. An educational video about the reef ecosystem is shown before entry.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Pass
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in the rich cultures of Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand through live demonstrations, canoe rides, and traditional performances. The evening luau and fire knife dance show is a highlight that kids and adults absolutely love.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a beginner family surf lesson on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered one of the best places in the world to learn to surf. Certified instructors guide kids and adults alike, and most first-timers stand up on their board within the first lesson. Boards and rash guards are included.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive & Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on a breathtaking self-guided road trip along Maui's famous Road to Hana, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and scenic lookouts. Families can swim at Twin Falls and explore the Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach State Park. Pack a picnic and make a full day of this unforgettable adventure.

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch at Helena's Hawaiian Food
experiences.description: Treat the family to an authentic, award-winning Hawaiian plate lunch experience at this legendary James Beard Award-winning restaurant. Enjoy classic dishes like kalua pig, lomi salmon, poi, and haupia (coconut pudding) in a no-frills, local atmosphere that has been serving Hawaii's comfort food since 1946.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity from the resort (typically a chilled bottle of champagne and fresh tropical fruit platter). Take a quiet stroll along the moonlit beach to decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — recommended: fresh poke bowl, macadamia-crusted shrimp, and a tropical fruit plate from the 24-hour in-room dining menu

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge before departure. Request early check-in preparation so the suite is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential after a long travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort morning. After waking, take a private sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. Enjoy a full luxury breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Spend time getting acquainted with resort amenities — infinity pool, cabanas, and beach setup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach. Book a private family surf lesson with a certified instructor for a personalized, safe, and fun experience on the gentle rolling waves. Waikiki is considered the birthplace of modern surfing and is ideal for beginners of all ages. Lessons typically run 90 minutes to 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails at the beachfront bar. Watch the legendary Hawaiian sunset from your private cabana with mai tais and fresh-caught fish tacos. Enjoy a relaxed family dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh acai bowls, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, fresh-squeezed lilikoi juice, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Post-surf casual lunch at a Waikiki beachside restaurant such as Nobu Honolulu or House Without a Key — try the wagyu sliders and fresh ahi poke
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — recommended: fresh island fish, lobster, and a tropical dessert tasting

day_by_day.notes: Book private surf lessons in advance through the resort concierge to ensure a family-sized group slot. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously. Bring a change of clothes and towels for after surfing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling excursion at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries. Reserve timed entry tickets in advance (required). Explore crystal-clear waters teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and hundreds of tropical species. Hire a private guide for a premium guided snorkeling experience tailored to the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Hanauma Bay and enjoy a poolside afternoon at the resort. Take advantage of the resort's water sports offerings — paddleboarding, kayaking, or a private catamaran charter along the coastline. Alternatively, relax in private beachfront cabanas with butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a world-class sunset dinner cruise departing from Honolulu Harbor. Enjoy premium open bar, live Hawaiian music, and a gourmet dinner while watching the sun dip below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh tropical fruit, granola, and Kona coffee to go
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic lunch prepared by the resort's culinary team — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water packed in a luxury cooler
meals.dinner: Premium sunset dinner cruise — multi-course gourmet meal featuring fresh Hawaiian seafood, prime rib, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance timed-entry reservations — book at least 2 weeks ahead. Arrive early as the bay can reach capacity quickly. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel gear (or rent premium gear on-site), and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience at the Polynesian Cultural Center — begin with the morning arrival and explore the six authentic island villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations including fire-making, hula, and traditional canoe paddling. Perfect for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the afternoon canoe pageant on the waterway, watch live cultural performances, and participate in interactive activities. Upgrade to the Ambassador VIP package for reserved seating, exclusive behind-the-scenes tours, and a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a spectacular theatrical performance celebrating Polynesian culture, music, and dance. Enjoy the included Ali'i Luau dinner before the show with traditional Hawaiian cuisine served in a beautiful outdoor setting.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure — eggs your way, fresh pastries, tropical juices, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Dining at the Polynesian Cultural Center — Gateway Bar & Grill or the All-You-Can-Eat Buffet included with Ambassador package featuring Hawaiian, Polynesian, and American cuisine
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and traditional Hawaiian dishes with premium seating

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Honolulu — arrange a private luxury vehicle or resort-arranged transportation. The Ambassador VIP Day Pass is highly recommended for families as it includes priority seating and personalized service. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury helicopter tour over Oahu — take a private family helicopter tour soaring over Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Waimea Bay, and the stunning North Shore coastline. A breathtaking perspective of the island only accessible from the air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Helena's Hawaiian Food for an authentic Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch experience. This legendary James Beard Award-winning restaurant in Kalihi serves authentic Hawaiian comfort food that has been a local institution for decades. Try the pipikaula short ribs, lomi salmon, and haupia for dessert.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy the resort spa with a couples' or family wellness session. Book a traditional lomi lomi massage, a volcanic stone treatment, or a family spa package. End the evening with a private beachfire experience arranged by the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-room private breakfast service on your beachfront lanai — fresh fruit platters, eggs Benedict, avocado toast, and tropical smoothies
meals.lunch: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch at Helena's Hawaiian Food — pipikaula short ribs, lau lau, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia
meals.dinner: Private beachfire dining experience at the resort — curated menu of fresh Hawaiian seafood, grilled meats, and tropical desserts served under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour through a reputable operator such as Blue Hawaiian Helicopters or Sunshine Helicopters — request a private family charter for exclusivity. Helena's is a cash-only establishment and portions are generous. Arrive early as lines can form quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui (approximately 30 minutes) — arrange a private charter or first-class seats on Hawaiian Airlines. Check into a luxury day-use suite or partner resort in Maui, or simply store luggage and begin exploring. Start the Road to Hana Scenic Drive early for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana Scenic Drive & Waterfalls — stop at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, Wailua Falls, and the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park. Hire a private luxury tour guide with a premium SUV for a fully curated, stress-free experience that handles all logistics.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hana for a sunset dinner at a local gem before the return journey or overnight stay. Return to Maui's resort area or fly back to Oahu depending on itinerary preference. Alternatively, book a one-night stay in Hana at Travaasa Hana for a truly immersive experience.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh pastries, fruit, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside gourmet picnic curated by your private tour guide — fresh banana bread from Aunt Sandy's, tropical fruits, and local snacks along the Road to Hana
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hana Ranch Restaurant or a private chef experience in Hana — fresh local fish, farm-to-table vegetables, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles with over 600 curves and 59 bridges — a private guided tour is strongly recommended for families to maximize enjoyment without the stress of driving. Book the tour well in advance. Start early (before 7am) to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Oahu (if overnight in Maui) or begin a relaxed resort morning. Enjoy a private family surf and paddleboard session arranged through the resort's water sports concierge on the calm beachfront waters. Younger children can enjoy a private beach setup with sandcastle-building kits and supervised water play.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — hike to the summit of this iconic volcanic crater for panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean. The trail is approximately 1.6 miles round trip and suitable for families. Hire a private naturalist guide for an enriched educational experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar followed by a premium omakase dinner at a top Honolulu sushi restaurant such as Sushi Sasabune or Nobu Honolulu.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — Hawaiian sweet bread French toast, fresh poke, tropical smoothie bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch at the resort — wagyu burgers, fresh fish tacos, tropical salads, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at Nobu Honolulu or Sushi Sasabune — premium multi-course Japanese-Hawaiian fusion featuring the freshest local catch

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head State Monument requires advance reservations for entry — book online at the Hawaii DLNR website. Bring water, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes. The hike takes approximately 1.5 to 2 hours round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury catamaran sailing charter — spend the morning sailing along the Oahu coastline, swimming in secluded coves, snorkeling over vibrant reefs, and spotting spinner dolphins and sea turtles. A fully crewed private charter ensures a premium, personalized experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor National Memorial for a deeply moving and historically significant experience. Book a premium guided tour that includes the USS Missouri Battleship and the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum for a comprehensive visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a farewell-style luxury luau experience — either the resort's own luau event or a booking at the prestigious Paradise Cove Luau or Chief's Luau, featuring traditional Hawaiian music, hula performances, fire dancing, and a lavish feast.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast aboard the catamaran — fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and mimosas served by the crew
meals.lunch: Post-Pearl Harbor lunch at Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua or a premium restaurant near the memorial — fresh seafood, prime cuts, and Hawaiian sides
meals.dinner: Premium luau feast — kalua pig, poi, fresh fish, tropical salads, and coconut desserts with open bar

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance ticket reservations — book the premium guided tour package online well ahead of time. The catamaran charter should be booked through a reputable operator such as Sail Oahu or Dream Cruises. Bring light layers for the evening luau.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — visit the famous Banzai Pipeline and Sunset Beach, shop at the Haleiwa town boutiques and art galleries, and sample shave ice at the legendary Matsumoto Shave Ice. Arrange a private luxury SUV for the day for comfortable family travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final afternoon of pure luxury relaxation. Spend time at the infinity pool, book a family spa treatment, or enjoy a private beach bonfire setup with games, hammocks, and personalized butler service. Children can enjoy supervised resort kids' club activities.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private chef dinner experience in your beachfront suite or on a private section of the beach. A top local chef prepares a custom multi-course Hawaiian feast featuring the finest local ingredients — fresh Kona lobster, wagyu beef, locally grown vegetables, and a custom dessert.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — loco moco, fresh tropical fruit platters, acai bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: North Shore food trucks and local eateries in Haleiwa — Giovanni's shrimp truck, fresh poke bowls, and Matsumoto Shave Ice for dessert
meals.dinner: Private chef multi-course dinner in your suite or on the beach — Kona lobster, wagyu beef, locally sourced vegetables, and a custom Hawaiian dessert with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is approximately 35 miles from Honolulu — allow 1 hour each way. If visiting between November and February, world-class big wave surfing competitions may be occurring. Book the private chef experience through the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk and meditation along the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Complete any last-minute souvenir shopping at the resort boutique or nearby luxury shops — Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and Hawaiian jewelry make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort checkout with late checkout arranged through the concierge (typically available for luxury guests). Enjoy final pool or beach time until departure. Private luxury transfer to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport arranged by the resort. Arrive at the airport with ample time for a relaxed premium departure experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 10 extraordinary days in Hawaii. Use the airport's premium lounge for pre-flight relaxation and dining.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant — full Hawaiian spread with eggs your way, fresh tropical fruits, pastries, smoked salmon, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport — fresh poke bowl, salad, and tropical juice
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal service

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout (typically 2pm or later for premium guests) well in advance. Arrange private airport transfer the night before. Confirm all souvenir purchases and pack carefully. Ensure all resort charges are reviewed and settled before checkout. Consider joining the resort's loyalty program for future stays.
